articles.title: Morning Mail: One Nation’s undercover videos, Trump’s ‘unprecedented’ fortune, Farage v Binface
articles.description: Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here , and finish your day with our Afternoon Update newsletter Morning everyone. One Nation has recently published a string of “undercover” videos in which a party staffer attends leftwing protests and seeks to embarrass protesters in filmed interviews. It comes as Penny Wong condemns Hanson’s monocultural policy as “melancholic fantasy”. Plus, a third near-miss at Sydney airport is under investigation, and Donald Trump has been attacked for being “openly corrupt” in amassing a personal fortune during his second presidency. Last lauf | Dineth Fernando, a 13-year-old from Melbourne, has won the 2026 World Youth Scrabble Championship with words including “lauf” and “minceur”. He moved to Australia from Sri Lanka in February and English is not even his first language. Exclusive | The owners of a progressive social media page have accused One Nation of impersonating them at anti-Pauline Hanson rallies while shooting a series of “undercover” videos . Labor has escalated its pushback on One Nation’s surging political support, with the foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, labelling Pauline Hanson’s push for a monoculture a “melancholic fantasy” . Third near-miss | The transport safety watchdog is investigating another near-collision between two planes at Sydney airport – which occurred on the same day as one that made national news and raised concerns about air traffic control. Paying the price? | The buy now, pay later boom arrived in Australia promising to one day replace credit cards. But with growth slowing and players leaving the market, is it all over? Luca Ittimani reports . Bishop convicted | The former bishop of Broome has been convicted of sexually abusing two young Aboriginal men. Christopher Saunders, 76, who was known for hosting boozy shirts-off parties, was found guilty of 13 sexual offences. Continue reading...

articles.description: MANILA, Philippines — Amid ongoing discussions on how the government can remove system loss charges from consumers’ electricity bills, the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) on Thursday said eliminating at least nontechnical loss would be feasible. The ERC laid out this possibility during a Senate energy panel hearing when committee chair Sen. Erwin Tulfo directly asked the commission if removing nontechnical system loss would be viable, especially as energy companies continue to oppose removing system loss altogether.
